title: Topology-aware sequence slicing and pad elimination for latency-cost tradeoffs
creator: Aisha Patel
description:
Problem: Our current prefill+decode pipeline bins requests solely by token count which leaves significant padding waste for multimodal and chat workloads with high variance in sequence length. This leads to higher GPU memory usage, suboptimal kernel choice, and degraded P50/P95 latency under mixed traffic.

Goal: Implement a topology-aware sequence slicing + pad elimination pass in the request packer that groups requests by both effective compute topology and expected KV cache footprint, and then performs in-flight slice-fusion and soft-trimming to remove unnecessary padding without violating caller-visible context guarantees. Target a 20% token-cost reduction for median conversational traffic and <5% impact on generation quality/effects on SLOs (P95 latency, tail).

Scope: packer changes, new topology classifier, scheduling hints exposed to runtime for kernel selection, fallbacks for hardware/kernel incompatibilities, and end-to-end perf validation in our staging fleet.
success_criteria: 1) End-to-end token cost reduction >= 18% on the conversational benchmark (internal workload). 2) P50 latency unchanged or improved; P95 latency no worse than +5% under production mix. 3) No regressions in logprob/QA evals beyond 0.5% for redwood-verified models. 4) Rollout flag and metrics visible in Console; automatic fallback to current packer on errors.
notes: 2026-03-02: Spike completed — prototype in packer can identify three topology classes (short-chat, long-prefill, long-decode) based on token distribution + KV footprint estimate. Early microbench shows ~22% token transfer reduction when slice-fusion applied to short-chat class.

2026-03-04: Trade-off discussion with infra: slice-fusion increases per-request scheduling complexity; accepted design to emit lightweight scheduling hints instead of blocking the scheduler — hints are (topology, max_allowed_trim, expected_kv_bytes).

2026-03-05: QA flagged potential context-trimming correctness edge cases with system prompts. Added conservative guard: only apply soft-trim on suffix padding and if caller metadata does not mark message as 'pinned'.

2026-03-06: Benchmark on g4dn (A10G) vs p4d (A100): kernel selection improved by preferring tiled attention kernels for topology class 2; net inference throughput +12% on p4d, +8% on g4dn. Noted a 0.8% increase in generation error-rate for a specific long-form summarization set — investigating prompt boundary handling.

2026-03-08: Design review with PM/Design — approved rollout plan with canary at 5% traffic for two days, observability dashboards to include pad-saved tokens, trimmed-requests ratio, kernel-mismatch fallbacks. Design requested clear metric to show 'visible context loss' (we'll use deterministic prompt-hash diff sampling).
2026-03-09: Security review concluded no new surface area but need KMS audit for rollout flags in Private deployments — tracked as follow-up to ensure flag visibility respects customer RBAC.
testing_plan: Unit tests for packer heuristics, CI microbench harness for kernel selection permutations, integration test that validates trimmed outputs are byte-equivalent where semantics-preserving, and a staged canary run (5% -> 25% -> 100%) with automated rollback on (token-cost increase OR P95 latency > +5% OR generation quality regression > 0.5%).
follow_up: ENG-42210: Add deterministic sampling job to detect visible context loss across customer prompt sets
ENG-42301: Console dashboard: pad-savings and kernel-selection heatmap per model/route
PM-512: Update customer-facing docs and rollout notes for Dedicated and Private customers
